title: Full article: A Comparative Pharmacokinetic Assessment of a Novel Highly Bioavailable Curcumin Formulation with 95% Curcumin: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Crossover Study
abstract:

Various approaches have been used Citation(12,15–19) to overcome the poor absorption, rapid metabolism, and poor bioavailability of curcumin. These strategies have been reviewed and include formulations with liposomes, micelles, or interaction with macromolecules such as gelatin and polysaccharides such as γ-cyclodextrin Citation(21) and galactomammans Citation(12,32). Furthermore, various nanoparticulate preparations that have been developed include nanoemulsions, nanomicelles, dendrimers, conjugates, polymers, nanogels, and solid dispersions Citation(16–19).
When the study product is compared to curcumin complexed with γ-cyclodextrin (Cavacurmin) Citation(32), the Cmax/mg and AUC/mg ingested curcumin for the novel study product were approximately 18.7 and 5.2 times, respectively, greater for the novel CLDM product (Table 3).
The products that provide the closest absorption per milligram of curcumin to the CLDM study product are the microparticle and surface-controlled colloidal dispersion technology product using ghatti gum and glycerin (Theracurmin) and the complex with fenugreek-derived galactomannan fiber (CurQfen).
